artists.biography:
CSS, short for Cansei de Ser Sexy, is a Brazilian band from São Paulo formed in 2003, known for turning a mix of electroclash, indie rock, dance-punk, and new rave energy into a loud, playful, club-ready style. Their name comes from a Portuguese phrase meaning “tired of being sexy,” and their bilingual approach and fashion-forward image helped make them stand out in the 2000s alternative dance scene.

The band’s breakthrough came with their self-titled debut album, released in Brazil in 2005 and internationally in 2006, which featured the infectious single “Let’s Make Love and Listen to Death from Above.” They followed it with Donkey in 2008, then La Liberación in 2011 and Planta in 2013, building a reputation for wiry synths, sharp rhythms, and irreverent lyrics. CSS became one of the most visible Brazilian exports of the electroclash and new rave era, helping bring Latin American indie dance music to a wider global audience.

apple_music.editorial_notes: While representing in Portuguese, these Brazilian rabble-rousers are just as playfully snarky in English. Right out of the gate, CSS's euphoric electro-rock drips with sleaze and sass, as hard-edged beats fuel ecstatic chants on "C.S.S. Suxxx". From there, they gleefully mock celebrity ("Meeting Paris Hilton") and find pleasure in their most favourite things with the deliriously catchy nu-disco of "Let's Make Love and Listen to Death from Above" and the crunchy guitar groove of "Music Is My Hot, Hot Sex".

perplexity.description:
Cansei De Ser Sexy is the chaotic, high-spirited self-titled debut from Brazilian outfit CSS, a record that helped define their blend of electroclash, dance-punk, and indie rock. Originally released in 2005 and later issued internationally through Sub Pop, the album captures the band’s mischievous, brash aesthetic with brittle synths, jagged guitars, propulsive beats, and Lovefoxxx’s playful, taunting vocals. Its best-known songs turned irony, club energy, and DIY attitude into something gleefully immediate and irresistibly catchy.

This 20th Anniversary reissue on colored vinyl revisits the album that brought CSS global attention, celebrating its place in the mid-2000s wave of danceable rock crossover. Reception at the time was largely positive, with critics praising its energy, wit, and hook-heavy momentum even when noting its deliberately raw, non-polished edges. The result is a snapshot of a band that sounded both irreverent and iconic, and the reissue highlights why the album remains such a defining statement in Sub Pop’s catalog.
